_: Everything this pipeline says out loud. Public-safe by design: account IDs and keys live in ~/.secrets, td-sops/apps/mwk-social.enc.env and ~/.zernio/config.json, never here.
_marker: The PRIMARY duplicate-guard substring, and the one every plain composed comment contains. Changing it is a breaking change: the watcher would stop recognising its own past comments and would comment again on every post.
markers: the link is on my channel page
_markers: EVERY substring that means 'this post already carries our CTA'. The guard matches any of them, which is the only reason the short link could be introduced at all: comments posted before it exists carry the long URL forever, and a guard that knew only the new one would re-comment on every past post. 'matewishkey.com/' joined on 2026-09-22, when a post first pointed somewhere other than the show: under the current voice the CTA IS a mention of his site, so 'does this comment already link to his site' is exactly the right question, and without it the watcher would add a second comment under every post that names a project page. 'link in my bio' joined on 2026-08-22 for the same reason in reverse — on Instagram and TikTok a url is not clickable at all, so those comments carry no URL to match on, and without this marker the watcher would re-comment on every one of them for ever.

shortLink._: One code per (platform, clip), minted through the dashboard's ingest API and idempotent — a re-run must render the identical comment or the guard above breaks. If minting fails the plain links.show is used instead: a link we cannot measure is far better than a comment that never goes out.

tags._always: Every post, in this order, spelled exactly as he typed them (mate, 2026-09-22: "our new tags always have to be #piyshow #mwkshow #PromptItYourself" — he is buying the domains). This REVERSES the 2026-08 pair (#MWKShow #PIY) and the earlier call that Prompt it Yourself is a sentence rather than a tag. Three always-on tags leave Instagram two topic slots, Pinterest none, and X carries only #piyshow — his cost, his call. Nothing re-tags what is already published.
tags._caps: null = no meaningful cap. Instagram's 5 is Instagram's; that it counts the caption AND the comments TOGETHER is not — that traces to marketing blogs and was retracted 2026-08-24. The behaviour stayed (tags go in one place, never both) because it costs nothing if the stricter reading turns out to be right. docs/playbook.md carries the full retraction. Pinterest's 3 is ours: its search reads the words, and a wall of tags in an 800-character description reads as spam.
tags._blocked: A hard stop, whatever the model returns. Three groups: the AI/tech category words that would appear on every video and say nothing; the engagement bait; and — added 2026-08-21 — DEVELOPER AND INFRASTRUCTURE VOCABULARY. That last group is the rule mate stated outright: tags are for normal humans, never for tech people. #Xero is fine because shop owners know it; #Cloudflare is not, because only we do.

firstComment._episodeMixRatio: 0 since 2026-09-22. The episode variants quoted a guest's wish and asked for yours, which is the pushing he stopped. The machinery is still in voice.js and the feed reader with it — an empty pool and a ratio of 0 mean neither is reached, and nothing curls the RSS for a comment any more.

profileCtaBy.youtube: the link is on my channel page

firstComment._profileCtaBy: Per-platform overrides of profileCta, for a surface where "my bio" is the wrong words. YouTube is the one so far: a url in a SHORT's description or comment is plain text, deliberately, to cut spam — but the CHANNEL's own links stay clickable and are YouTube's documented route out of a Short. Every value here MUST also be in markers[] above, exactly like profileCta, or the duplicate guard stops recognising a comment we wrote and the watcher comments again on every one of them for ever.
firstComment._profileCta: What {show} becomes on a platform where a url in a post or a comment is PLAIN TEXT but the BIO is live — Instagram alone since 2026-09-14, when TikTok moved to linkPlacement 'none': its bio link is plain text too on a personal account under 1,000 followers, so a TikTok post now says nothing about a link at all. Printing a tracked short code there burns a code nobody can click and reads in the numbers as 'posted, no interest' rather than 'never reachable': five TikTok codes took zero human clicks between them. This string MUST also appear in markers[] above, or the duplicate guard stops recognising these comments and the watcher re-comments on every one, for ever.
firstComment._register: Plain, correct English. Capitals, apostrophes and full stops as normal. This REVERSED an earlier decision to write informally on purpose — lowercase openings, dropped commas, 'dont' — which mate called on 2026-08-24: it read as careless rather than relaxed, and a comment under a video is the show's shop window. Warmth comes from the ROTATION and from what the sentences say, not from dropped punctuation. Still hand-written, never mangled at runtime, so every possible output has been read by a human. Never alter the URL and never break the marker. NOBODY IS ASKED TO COME (mate, 2026-09-22): he renamed /show to "Apply to be a guest" and said to drop the begging flavour — keep mwkshow.com, "stop using the beg to come, just mention the site, that's it". A variant now STATES something true and names the site. "Bring me yours", "come to the show" and "yours could be next" are gone. Applying is the site's own frame and is the opposite of begging: he picks every guest himself. AND THEN: JUST THE LINK (mate, 2026-09-22, an hour later). "We do not have to ask a question, just the link... we do not overcomplicate it. If they do not want to come I do not care, I do not want to push folks, only if they care." So the comment is the url and the topic tags, and nothing else. One variant is deliberate: the rotation, avoidIndex and the episode pool all still work and all have nothing to choose between. The CAPTION still ends on Prompt it yourself! — that is his own writing and the brand's argument; this is about the comment underneath.

youtubeDescription._showBlurbPast: Every blurb this channel has carried, newest first. findBlurb() matches the constant halves either side of {show}, so the DAY the wording above changes every description already written stops being recognised as ours — and an unrecognised blurb takes the full rebuild path, which regenerates the opening with a model. That is 23 re-approvals of words he already said yes to, as the price of one edit to a paragraph. Retiring a blurb means pushing the old text here, not deleting it. Nothing is ever removed from this list: a video written a year ago still carries the blurb of its day.
youtubeDescription._showBlurb: Written from matewishkey.com/brand, which is the authority on how the show describes itself — not a paraphrase of it. The brand page's rules are load-bearing here: first person, the viewer as the subject, plain language, no smugness, and the host is never positioned as expert or teacher. Never the words "free", "guaranteed" or "safe", and never a claim that anyone became a developer. Change this and every YouTube description changes with it. NO HASHTAGS HERE: yt-description.js appends voice.tagLine() after the blurb, so tags in this text print twice. AND NO SECOND ADDRESS: the 'Live on youtube.com/@matewishkey and twitch.tv/matewishkey' line was dropped on 2026-08-25 (mate: "why we are promoting twitch on the youtube live at all, they are already on youtube"). Half of it pointed at the platform the viewer was already on and the other half sent them to a different one — and on a Short it printed two urls directly under a CTA that had been denied a url on the grounds that urls do not work there. One address, and it is the one we want them to use.
